questions.answer: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is a strategic framework for making sure your brand appears in AI-generated search results and recommendations. It involves optimizing your digital footprint so AI systems like ChatGPT, Google's Search Generative Experience, and Perplexity recognize your brand as authoritative, relevant, and trustworthy enough to cite [6]. Compared with AEO, GEO is broader and longer term, aiming to make a brand a recognized entity that AI systems mention by name [5]. You can read more on the [FAQ page](/faq/) or the [AEO and GEO guide](/blog/what-is-aeo-and-geo-business-owners-guide-ai-search/).

questions.answer: SEO is a long-term investment, and timelines depend on your starting point, competition, and goals. Technical fixes and quick wins can show impact within weeks, while meaningful organic traffic growth typically appears between three and six months, and compounding results often show at six to twelve months [1]. For AEO and GEO, visibility in AI systems can shift faster [1]. Joe sets expectations based on each situation and gives ongoing progress updates [1].

questions.answer: An MCP server is the piece that lets Claude connect to outside tools and data. For example, it can let Claude read from a database, query an analytics account or take an action in another system [1]. The Model Context Protocol is an open standard for connecting AI applications to outside tools and data [2]. Joe usually sets this up read-only at first, with limits you choose [2]. questions.answer: Joe's site covers keyword research as a shift away from exact-match keywords toward user intent and conversational queries. Tools still matter, but they need to be supplemented with newer approaches that capture how people search today [4][1]. Useful methods include identifying intent with tools that classify it, studying "People Also Ask" results, and examining current search results for your target keywords [3][5].
